name: DatabaseCrashSpec
source_title: No canonical DatabaseCrash CrySL source was found: the explicitly requested raw primary-source URL returned HTTP 404 when fetched.
important_note: There is no verified API type or CrySL rule for DatabaseCrashSpec. The required applies_to_types entry is a syntactic unresolved placeholder whose simple name is exactly DatabaseCrash; it must not be treated as an existing Java/Android API or as a type actually governed by a specification. The two reported call sites belong to different application classes, and neither class has the required simple name DatabaseCrash.

events.name: reported_database_operation
events.condition: Observed when local source, a stack trace, or a detector record contains either reported method-call substring. Observation alone does not establish a database crash, a failed transaction, or that either method threw an exception.

events.name: unique_constraint_exception_evidence
events.condition: Satisfied only when exception evidence identifies SQLiteConstraintException together with the reported unique-constraint message. Android documents SQLiteConstraintException as an integrity-constraint violation; it is not documentation of database-file corruption or an application crash.

events.name: database_corruption_exception_evidence
events.condition: Satisfied only when exception evidence identifies SQLiteDatabaseCorruptException together with the reported malformed-image message. Android documents that exception as indicating a corrupt SQLite database file; it does not, by itself, establish the corruption cause, recoverability, persistence of damage, or process termination.

events.name: unresolved_spec_target
events.condition: Observed only as a requested CrySL target-name token. It is not satisfied as an API-target predicate: no consulted primary source defines a qualified API type named DatabaseCrash or a CrySL SPEC declaration for it.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That eu.kanade.tachiyomi.data.database.MangaDatabase.insertChapter caused, observed, or can repair database-file corruption.
That com.ichi2.anki.provider.DeckManager.syncDecks caused the malformed SQLite image rather than merely encountering it.
That SQLiteConstraintException means a database crash, corruption, disk failure, or security incident.
That a UNIQUE constraint failure on chapters.url and a SQLiteDatabaseCorruptException have one shared database, code path, root cause, or remediation.
That either reported application class is the API governed by DatabaseCrashSpec.
That unresolved.DatabaseCrash exists in Android, the Java platform, Tachiyomi, AnkiDroid, or the CROSSINGTUD corpus.
That the detector establishes exploitability, confidentiality impact, integrity impact beyond the reported SQLite condition, availability impact, or a successful runtime crash.
semantic_scope: The available evidence supports only classification of two reported SQLite-related exception/message shapes in two distinct application-method contexts: a unique-constraint violation at insertChapter and a database-corruption exception at syncDecks. It does not provide a verified CrySL protocol, an API contract for either application method, or a verified DatabaseCrash API type.

detector_semantics.claim: A DatabaseCrashSpec finding can only be described, on the supplied evidence, as a detector label associated with a reported database-operation context and SQLite exception/message evidence; its formal rule predicates are unverified because the requested canonical CrySL source was unavailable.
predicates: call_context_observed: a finding identifies either MangaDatabase.insertChapter or DeckManager.syncDecks.
constraint_message_observed: the evidence contains SQLiteConstraintException and the UNIQUE constraint failed: chapters.url text.
corruption_message_observed: the evidence contains SQLiteDatabaseCorruptException and the database disk image is malformed text.
verified_crysl_target: unavailable; no consulted primary source establishes a SPEC whose governed qualified type has simple name DatabaseCrash.
limitations: No source-defined event alphabet, ORDER clause, CONSTRAINTS clause, REQUIRES clause, ENSURES clause, or exception predicate was available for DatabaseCrashSpec.
Method-name matching is not proof that the method was executed, that the shown exception propagated from it, or that a particular database instance was affected.
The supplied findings are insufficient to determine whether matching is static, log-based, trace-based, interprocedural, path-sensitive, or runtime-confirmed.

documented_behavior: Android documents android.database.sqlite.SQLiteConstraintException as an integrity-constraint violation and android.database.sqlite.SQLiteDatabaseCorruptException as indicating that the SQLite database file is corrupt. Both are SQLiteException subclasses.
preconditions: For the unique-constraint interpretation, the reported exception/message must be authentic runtime evidence from the relevant SQLite operation and database.
For the database-corruption interpretation, the reported exception/message must be authentic runtime evidence from SQLite rather than a copied, wrapped, synthesized, or stale log string.

No primary source was located for the behavior, parameters, transaction boundaries, error handling, or persistence guarantees of the reported MangaDatabase.insertChapter and DeckManager.syncDecks methods.
unknowns: Whether insertChapter and syncDecks are exact source-level declarations for the builds that produced the findings.

security_semantics.detector_claim: Unverified. No primary DatabaseCrash CrySL rule was available to establish a security property, misuse definition, or security-relevant protocol.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: The reported SQLiteConstraintException supports an integrity-constraint violation at an operation; the reported SQLiteDatabaseCorruptException supports that SQLite identified a database file as corrupt. Neither documented exception classification alone proves a security vulnerability or a process crash.

known_false_positive_shapes: A local matcher sees insertChapter( or syncDecks( but the method was never executed on the analyzed path.
A log, test fixture, comment, exception wrapper, or telemetry payload contains one of the SQLite exception substrings without a corresponding runtime exception.
SQLiteConstraintException is labeled as a crash even though Android defines it as an integrity-constraint violation.
The malformed-image text is historical, copied from another device/database, or emitted after the database had already been replaced or recovered.
Two independent findings from separate applications/components are merged into one supposed DatabaseCrash event.
A namesake type ending in Spec, or a type from another framework, is selected despite not being a qualified API type whose simple name is DatabaseCrash.

The actual qualified API type intended by the DatabaseCrash name; no authoritative type definition was found.
